Project Charter
Sangha and Education Data Platform
Item | Details
Document | Project Charter for owner review
Version | 0.1
Document status | Proposal — not approval to build or use real data
Data boundary | Synthetic data only; no real persons, contact data, applicants, or official records
Architecture | Confirmed — use the approved architecture; this charter adds no components

This charter defines a synthetic-data product foundation for structured Sangha and education records. It covers role directories, organisations, exam centres, organisational status, and learner-exam applicant workflows. Server-side authorisation and append-only history are non-negotiable.
Status Labels
Label | Meaning
Confirmed | Requirement verified in the work request or approved architecture context.
Proposal | Recommended product decision for owner approval before detailed design or implementation.
Needs Legal Review | Potential effect on data rights, official status, disclosure, or external requirements; requires authorised legal or compliance review.

1 Product Scope
Status | In scope | Charter outcome
Confirmed | Education-leadership directory at every approved level | Synthetic directory records can show role, organisation, term, and relationship.
Confirmed | Secretaries linked to a role or organisation | Role support and assignment periods are traceable.
Confirmed | Head of institution or principal and education organisations | Role and organisation relationships are managed through approved data structures.
Confirmed | Exam centres and organisation status | Synthetic centres, lifecycle status, and status history are managed.
Confirmed | Learner and exam applicants | Synthetic applications and application status history are managed.
Confirmed | Server-side authorisation and append-only history | Protected reads and writes are checked on the server; changes do not overwrite history.
Proposal | Synthetic import template with pre-save validation | A reviewer can identify row-level errors before committing a mock-data import.

2 Goals and Non Goals
Type | Status | Decision
Goal | Confirmed | Create a role-based data foundation for organisations, education roles, exam centres, and synthetic applicants.
Goal | Confirmed | Enable the owner to review role-based access and end-to-end status history.
Goal | Proposal | Provide a completeness view for synthetic records and items awaiting review.
Non Goal | Confirmed | Do not collect, migrate, connect, or process real personal data in this phase.
Non Goal | Confirmed | Do not issue credentials, determine exam eligibility, or publish official results.
Non Goal | Confirmed | Do not replace owner-controlled approval processes or official regulations.
Non Goal | Needs Legal Review | Do not publish a directory or applicant data without a reviewed disclosure basis.

3 Role Based Stakeholders
Role | Status | Responsibility | Expected synthetic-environment access
Product Owner | Confirmed | Approves scope, priorities, role taxonomy, and acceptance criteria. | View all modules; approve configuration decisions.
Data Steward | Proposal | Defines identifiers, required fields, data quality rules, and master-data review. | Manage permitted master data.
Education Directory Manager | Proposal | Reviews organisations, leadership roles, secretaries, and institution leadership. | Submit change requests and view history.
Exam Operations Officer | Proposal | Reviews exam centres and synthetic applicant workflow. | Manage permitted centre and workflow data.
Applicant Services Officer | Proposal | Exercises synthetic registration and status follow-up. | Read and update status only within role policy.
System Administrator | Confirmed | Administers identities, roles, settings, and recovery procedure. | Manage access without deleting business history.
Security Reviewer | Proposal | Reviews server enforcement, audit events, and recovery evidence. | Read audit records and actual test evidence.
Legal or Compliance Reviewer | Needs Legal Review | Determines real-data, disclosure, retention, and user-notice obligations. | No operating access is implied by this charter.

4 Data and Authorisation Principles
Confirmed — All samples must be fictional and clearly non-identifying. The initial environment remains separate from any real source.
Confirmed — Every protected read, create, status change, and history access is authorised on the server. Hiding a user-interface option is not a sufficient control.
Confirmed — Every change records actor, role, timestamp, before and after values, reason, and relevant request identifier. A correction creates a new version or event; it must not overwrite history.
Proposal — Use logical deactivation such as inactive or superseded for business records, with a reason. Permit synthetic test-data cleanup only through a separate privileged procedure that records an event.
5 Glossary
Term | Working definition
Organisation | An education body or unit in the owner-approved structure. This charter does not assert any real organisation or official status.
Education leadership role | A directory role linked to a level or organisation and a term of office.
Secretary | A support role linked to a role, organisation, or both, as approved in the data model.
Head of institution or principal | A neutral prototype term for a role responsible for an institution or education unit.
Exam centre | A synthetic exam location record with identifier, lifecycle status, stated capacity, and exam-cycle relationship.
Learner and exam applicant | A fictional applicant record used to test registration and status workflow.
Organisation status | Lifecycle control such as draft, active, suspended, or superseded; actual values require owner confirmation.
Append-only history | Event record that adds a new entry and is not changed or removed through normal operations.

6 Assumptions and Open Questions
Status | Topic | Current answer or decision required | Owner to confirm
Confirmed | Initial data | Synthetic data only and separated from real source systems. | Product Owner
Proposal | Leadership taxonomy | Use configurable master data; do not encode real names or unverified hierarchy. | Product Owner and Data Steward
Proposal | Secretary relationship | A secretary may link to a role, an organisation, or both; confirm cardinality and effective dates. | Product Owner
Proposal | Applicant lifecycle | Start with draft, submitted, under review, approved, and not approved; no official effect. | Exam Operations Owner
Needs Legal Review | Allowed real-data categories | Define data categories, permitted basis, notices, and access controls before any real-data use. | Legal or Compliance Reviewer
Needs Legal Review | Retention and history rights | Define retention, log access, and data-subject handling before real-data use. | Legal or Compliance Reviewer
Needs Legal Review | Official status definitions | Do not state or publish a real organisation or exam-centre status until an authorised body confirms it. | Authorised Business Owner

7 Success Metrics and Acceptance Evidence
All metrics below are proposals, not test results. Delivery must name the test case, evidence owner, pass threshold, and actual result.
Status | Metric | Proposed threshold | Required evidence
Proposal | Synthetic workflow coverage | Owner reviews all six data groups: directory, secretary, institution leadership, organisation, centre, applicant. | Owner acceptance checklist.
Proposal | Authorisation enforcement | Every in-scope protected endpoint has one allow and one deny test against the role matrix. | Actual automated or recorded test results.
Proposal | History integrity | A representative correction creates before-and-after history without overwriting an older event. | Actual test result and audit-event example.
Proposal | Failure recovery | Run agreed scenarios for write, permission, and import failures. | Runbook and actual recovery exercise result.
Proposal | Synthetic data quality | Each mock-data set passes required-field, duplicate-id, and referential rules. | Validation report from synthetic data.

8 Dependencies
Status | Dependency | Impact if unavailable | Confirmation owner
Confirmed | Approved architecture and synthetic-environment deployment route | No new component may be introduced in conflict with approved architecture. | Technical Owner
Proposal | Owner-approved role matrix and taxonomy | Data model relationships and access policy cannot be finalised. | Product Owner
Proposal | Synthetic data set and validation rules | End-to-end workflow cannot be exercised. | Data Steward
Proposal | Audit-event design and recovery runbook | History and recovery readiness cannot be demonstrated. | Security Reviewer and Technical Owner
Needs Legal Review | Approval for future real-data or public-disclosure use | The product must remain synthetic-only and disconnected from real data. | Legal or Compliance Reviewer

9 Failure Modes and Recovery
Failure mode | Prevention or detection | Recovery | Status
Write request lacks permission | Server authorises before transaction and logs the denial. | Do not change data; provide safe reason; review role mapping. | Confirmed
Business write fails while creating history | Commit business data and audit event atomically, or roll both back. | Roll back; inspect error record; retry using idempotency key. | Proposal
Synthetic import contains duplicate ID or invalid relationship | Validate before commit and report row-level errors. | Reject invalid rows; correct source; re-import; retain import attempt. | Proposal
Authorised user makes an incorrect status change | Require reason and confirmation; always create a new event. | Create corrective event or a new state version; do not edit old event. | Confirmed
Access policy changes during a session | Refresh permission source for sensitive operations. | Revoke risky session; require authorisation again; inspect audit trail. | Proposal
Real data is imported through the wrong route | Separate environments and check synthetic-data marker before import. | Stop import; quarantine set; notify owner; await legal or compliance direction. | Needs Legal Review

10 Owner Review Checklist
Approval should follow owner review of the items below. Actual test results are recorded only after tests are run.
☐ Confirm the six scoped data groups and delivery order.
☐ Confirm leadership taxonomy and secretary relationship rule.
☐ Confirm minimum role matrix and status-change approvers.
☐ Confirm lifecycle states for organisation, exam centre, and applicant mock data.
☐ Select acceptance evidence for authorisation, history, and recovery.
☐ Send all Needs Legal Review items for authorised review before real-data use or public disclosure.
11 Initial Decision Log
Decision | Status | Reason | Change condition
Use synthetic data only in charter phase | Confirmed | Avoids personal-data risk and unauthorised real-data use. | Only with written owner and legal or compliance approval.
Enforce authorisation on the server | Confirmed | Interface visibility is not a sufficient access control. | Requires a new security review to change.
Keep append-only history | Confirmed | Supports traceability and reversible correction. | Schema may change, but prior events may not be overwritten.
Use logical deactivation for business records | Proposal | Preserves history and supports recovery. | Owner confirms model and retention treatment.
Public disclosure or real-data use | Needs Legal Review | Affects data rights and official status beyond this charter. | Authorised review and approval required before start.

Verification Note
This is a Project Charter, not a test report. It does not claim that any system, import, or recovery activity has been run. Future evidence must include date, executor, environment, test case, and actual outcome.

RBAC and Scope Security Architecture
Sangha and Education Data Platform
Item | Security design statement
Purpose | Deny-by-default authorization design for protected website actions and reads across geographic and organisation boundaries.
Architecture alignment | Confirmed: Auth.js; Prisma/PostgreSQL; protected Server Actions/API routes; server-side role-and-scope authorization; atomic domain/history/audit writes.
Core rule | A request is allowed only when session, account state, action, active role grant, scope chain, target resource and workflow policy all resolve positively.
Boundary | Synthetic fictional data only. This design does not create legal authority, retention periods or permission to release real personal information.
Verification target | Cross-scope request must return 403 from the server. The document specifies tests; it does not claim those product tests have run.
Status Labels
Label | Meaning
Confirmed | Approved architecture or non-negotiable security constraint.
Proposal | Control or role policy to confirm before implementation and owner review.
Needs Legal Review | Authority, delegation, official publication, retention or real-data decision requiring evidence and review.

1 Authorization Decision Model
The application must not derive authority from a screen, route visibility, browser state or client-supplied organisation identifier. Each protected Server Action, API route, export and file retrieval repeats the authorization decision using trusted server-side data.

Decision input | Required server handling | Status
Session and account | Validate authenticated session, account active state and request correlation ID. Unauthenticated requests receive 401; authenticated but unauthorized requests receive 403. | Confirmed
Action | Map endpoint/server action to a controlled action code. Do not accept an action code from the client. | Confirmed
Role grant | Resolve current active user_role_scope_grant and its append-only grant events. A stale, revoked or expired grant is insufficient. | Proposal
Geographic and org scope | Resolve the permitted geographic node and organisation subtree from trusted scope records; intersect with the resource scope. | Proposal
Resource and workflow state | Check target ownership, classification, current event-derived state and maker-checker separation before querying or writing. | Confirmed
Response | Return only allow-listed fields. On failure, return a safe 403 with no target existence, scope or sensitive-field disclosure. | Confirmed
2 Scope Model
Scope is a conjunctive boundary: the request must satisfy every scope dimension attached to the action. A wider UI view never widens a server-side grant.
Scope dimension | Representation and matching rule | Examples using synthetic labels | Status
Geographic | Geo node with ancestor path; a grant may match its node and confirmed descendants only. No implicit sibling or parent expansion. | Region R1; Province P01; District D01 | Proposal
Organisation | organisation_id hierarchy in the ERD. A grant matches the approved organisation subtree, not every organisation with a similar name. | Organisation O100; School S200; Exam Centre C300 | Proposal
Functional | Action family restricts domain use even inside a matching geography/org scope. | application.review; import.submit; audit.read | Confirmed
Data class | Field projection policy determines which columns/files may be returned after action/scope approval. | Internal vs Highly Restricted | Confirmed
Time and state | Grant effective range and event-derived workflow state must be valid at decision time. | active grant; submitted application | Confirmed
3 Role and Action Baseline
Role | Permitted action families inside scope | Explicitly denied | Status
Product Owner | policy.review; dashboard.aggregate.read; approval.request | private record read; role grant change; operational approval | Proposal
Data Steward | directory.read/write; org.status.propose; import.review | grant own role; approve own change; unrestricted export | Proposal
Education Directory Manager | education.directory.read/write; position.propose; secretary.propose | exam decision; access grant change; out-of-scope organisation | Proposal
Exam Operations Officer | exam.session/centre.read/write; application.review; candidate status propose | private person contact read; approve own import or decision | Proposal
Applicant Services Officer | application.read/write for assigned scope; document intake | legal review; final approval; cross-scope application read | Proposal
System Administrator | system.configuration; role grant request; security event view | business data bypass; self-approval; raw private export by default | Confirmed
Security Reviewer | audit.read; grant/history review; access review recommendation | operational mutation; role grant activation; private-document download | Confirmed
Legal Compliance Reviewer | legal.mapping/review; evidence metadata review | operational record mutation; broad candidate/person data access | Needs Legal Review

4 Maker Checker and Approval Controls
Maker-checker applies where a change could alter access, official status, published projection, high-risk data treatment or an evidence-backed decision. The exact authority matrix remains subject to owner and legal review.
Control | Maker restriction | Checker requirement | Evidence and history | Status
Role or scope grant | Requester cannot activate, extend or revoke own grant; administrator initiates a request only. | A separately authorized checker confirms grant scope, purpose and effective dates. | Append grant request, decision event and audit record; never overwrite a grant. | Proposal
Organisation or position status | Maker may propose a status event in scope. | Checker must be different user and have action plus target scope. | Append approval_decision_event then status event in one transaction. | Proposal
Application decision | Reviewer may prepare decision and evidence links. | Checker is a distinct user; same-user approval rejected even if both roles are held. | Append application_status_event and audit; correction is later event. | Confirmed
Import promotion | Importer cannot approve rows from own job into protected records. | Checker validates errors, scope, schema version and source condition. | Keep import_job, row errors and promotion audit trace. | Proposal
Public projection release | Maker creates release candidate only. | Independent release approver and legal gate when content requires it. | Versioned release decision and audit; source tables remain private. | Needs Legal Review
5 Privilege Escalation Controls
Threat | Mandatory control | Detection and recovery | Status
Client changes organisation or geography ID | Ignore client scope claims. Load target resource and scope from server-side IDs; intersect with active grant. | Return 403; audit denied action with redacted target reference; investigate repeated attempts. | Confirmed
Role selection in UI | Role picker is presentation only. Server maps actor to current grants; no client role header or cookie is trusted. | Return 403; revoke/expire only through append-only checker workflow. | Confirmed
Self approval or checker reuse | Enforce maker_user_id <> checker_user_id and decision actor uniqueness within the same decision chain. | Reject transaction; retain attempt audit; use another checker. | Proposal
Admin bypass of business scope | System administration is not a business-data super-role. Require explicit time-bounded support grant, reason and checker approval. | Default 403; log support session; automatic expiry and post-review. | Proposal
Token/session replay or stale grant | Short session policy and server re-check of account/grant validity on every protected call. | Invalidate session or grant event; force re-authentication; reconcile audit trail. | Proposal
Bulk export or document exfiltration | Separate export/download actions; enforce field projection, scope, rate/volume policy and private object authorization. | Stop job/revoke link; preserve audit; assess with owner/DPO/legal if real data involved. | Needs Legal Review
6 Transaction and Audit Rules
Operation | Atomic transaction requirement | Audit minimum | Status
Protected write | Authorize then write domain row, status/decision event and audit_event together; rollback all on any failure. | actor, action, scope resolution outcome, target type/id, request ID, timestamp and result. | Confirmed
Denied request | Do not create business/history records. A permitted security audit may record the denied action without sensitive values. | actor/session reference where available, action, safe target reference, 403 outcome. | Confirmed
Grant or escalation | Write request, checker decision, effective grant event and audit together. | maker/checker, before/after scope code, reason reference, expiry and decision. | Proposal
Correction | Insert a later correction/revocation/reinstatement event; never UPDATE/DELETE historical business or grant event. | links to prior event and correction reason reference. | Confirmed
7 Negative Access Test Specification
All tests below are required product tests. “Expected 403” means the protected server endpoint/action must reject without returning data, mutation confirmation or existence-disclosing error detail. They are not recorded as executed in this document.
Test ID | Actor role | Attempt | Expected server result | Status
NEG 01 | Product Owner | Read a Highly Restricted candidate_private record using dashboard permission. | 403; no record fields or existence signal. | Proposal
NEG 02 | Data Steward | Write organisation status outside granted organisation subtree. | 403; no status event; denied audit permitted. | Proposal
NEG 03 | Education Directory Manager | Read or mutate an exam centre in a sibling geographic branch. | 403; cross-scope=403. | Proposal
NEG 04 | Exam Operations Officer | Read person_contact or candidate_private without explicit private-data action. | 403; no private projection. | Proposal
NEG 05 | Applicant Services Officer | Approve an application they prepared or read another organisation’s application. | 403; no approval/status event. | Proposal
NEG 06 | System Administrator | Invoke business-data export using system configuration authority only. | 403; no export job or object link. | Proposal
NEG 07 | Security Reviewer | Activate or extend own role/scope grant. | 403; no grant event. | Proposal
NEG 08 | Legal Compliance Reviewer | Read broad candidate list or mutate application status. | 403; no private data or mutation. | Proposal
NEG 09 | Any authenticated role | Submit client-supplied role/action/scope that is stronger than server grant. | 403; server ignores untrusted claim. | Confirmed
NEG 10 | Any authenticated role | Use direct ID of record in another geo/org scope (IDOR). | 403; cross-scope=403. | Confirmed
NEG 11 | Any authenticated role | Call protected endpoint with expired/revoked grant. | 403; no data or mutation. | Proposal
NEG 12 | Maker with checker role | Approve own same decision via a second browser/session. | 403; maker-checker conflict. | Proposal
NEG 13 | Importer | Promote own import job into protected rows. | 403; no promotion transaction. | Proposal
NEG 14 | Public caller | Request private API/document key by guessing path or ID. | 401/403 according to authentication state; no object bytes. | Confirmed
8 Failure Modes and Recovery
Failure mode | Fail closed response | Recovery | Status
Scope resolver unavailable or ambiguous | 403; do not fall back to broader organisation or geographic access. | Restore trusted scope data; retry only after a fresh server decision; investigate affected audit records. | Confirmed
Audit/event insert fails | Rollback protected mutation and return a safe failure. | Reconcile from committed state only; no manual overwrite of history. | Confirmed
Checker identity unavailable | Do not approve or activate grant/status/release. | Assign an eligible independent checker; preserve pending request. | Proposal
Suspected real data in test/import/document | Quarantine processing and block release. | Notify designated owner/DPO/legal reviewer; do not certify any compliance outcome. | Needs Legal Review
Break-glass requested | No implicit bypass. Require pre-defined, time-bound, checked emergency path before use. | Expire access automatically; review every action and append outcome. | Proposal
9 Owner Review Checklist
Review item | Decision needed | Status
Role catalogue | Confirm final role names, action families and whether any combined roles are permitted. | Proposal
Scope hierarchy | Confirm geographic levels, organisation tree ownership and descendant inheritance rules. | Proposal
Maker checker | Confirm actions that require independent approval and allowed exception authority. | Needs Legal Review
Emergency support | Approve or reject a time-bound support/break-glass policy, retention and reviewers. | Needs Legal Review
Negative tests | Run cross-scope=403 and all relevant IDOR, self-approval and private-data tests in implementation. | Proposal

Sitemap and User Flows
Sangha and Education Data Platform
Item | Details
Purpose | Route, navigation, page and flow design for synthetic-data operation. It tells each role where to go and what state to expect without treating the interface as a security control.
Scope | Leadership/education directory, organisations, exam centres, applicants, imports, audit, access and legal/publication review. Only fictional non-identifying data is in scope.
Main decision | Public routes read a dedicated release-gated projection. Private routes are capability-led. Every protected read and mutation is authorised on the server.
Verification method | Actor walkthrough design review. No implemented UI, API authorisation policy or product walkthrough is claimed as tested.
Status Labels
Label | Meaning
Confirmed | Established architectural or requirement constraint. It does not make a record public or grant a role access.

R-12 | /app/imports | Data Steward | Start synthetic CSV/XLSX import and review job summary. | Import is private; no raw rejected values in list. | Confirmed

4 Page States and Recovery
State | When it appears | Required UX behaviour | Server or recovery behaviour | Status

Validation error | User submits missing/invalid synthetic input. | Show field-level error with preserved safe input; do not expose policy internals. | Reject mutation; no status/history event written until valid. | Confirmed
Action error | Network/service/transaction issue during protected action. | Show retry guidance and stable request reference; do not say an approval succeeded. | Use atomic rollback; reconcile via latest server state/audit event. | Confirmed

Failure mode | Containment | Recovery | Status

Public route serialises protected field | Disable route/projection cache and withdraw candidate. | Correct allow-list, regenerate projection, inspect access logs, require owner/legal review. | Needs Legal Review
History/audit transaction fails | Do not show successful mutation. | Roll back related write; retry only after server can atomically write business/history/audit events. | Confirmed
Import contains suspected real data | Stop workflow before confirm. | Quarantine private file, notify designated owner/DPO/legal reviewer; do not certify outcome. | Needs Legal Review

F-07 | System Administrator | Access -> identify change request -> validate policy -> create role-change event -> revoke/reissue session as configured. | Server validates administrator scope; no client-supplied role is trusted. | Proposal

F-10 | Legal Compliance Reviewer | Legal Mapping -> review TO VERIFY/evidence record -> record role-based outcome -> hand back to owner. | Legal role does not gain operating-data authority; outcome is append-only. | Proposal

Capability or requirement | UI and routes | Server boundary | History and audit consequence | Status

Application workflow | /app/my-applications; /app/applications/[id] | Self-service bind or workflow-role scope check before query/action. | Application status event appended; reviewer/audit data withheld from applicant. | Confirmed

documents.text:
Solution Architecture
Sangha and Education Data Platform
Item | Architecture statement
Outcome | A secure modular-monolith web platform with protected server actions/API routes, append-only history and governed asynchronous processing.
Confirmed baseline | Next.js App Router, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Auth.js, private object storage, queue/jobs and CDN/WAF.
Security boundary | Authorization is evaluated on the server by action, role, active grant, geographic/org scope, data class and workflow state. UI never grants access.
Data boundary | Only synthetic fictional data is within scope. Object bytes are private; PostgreSQL holds minimal document metadata and explicit links.
Review method | Architecture review of the logical design. No deployment, migration, backup restore, load, security scan or product test is claimed as executed.
Status Labels
Label | Meaning
Confirmed | Approved architecture or mandatory design boundary.
Proposal | Implementation detail or operating target requiring owner confirmation.
Needs Legal Review | Authority, real-data use, retention, public release or evidence decision requiring review.

1 Target Architecture
The target is a modular monolith. Next.js serves public and private experiences, while domain modules centralize policy enforcement, transaction orchestration and event/audit creation. Background workers execute only committed work through a queue; they do not substitute for a successful protected write.

Layer | Responsibility | Boundary | Status
Edge | CDN cache for approved public assets; WAF and rate limits before origin. | No private data cache; protected responses set no-store/private. | Proposal
Web | Next.js App Router, route handlers and Server Actions in TypeScript. | No direct client authorization or database credentials. | Confirmed
Domain | Policy checks, validation, maker-checker and transaction orchestration. | Shared server-only modules; deny by default. | Confirmed
Data | PostgreSQL accessed through Prisma; event tables derive current state. | No overwrite of business history; protected migrations only. | Confirmed
Objects | Private object storage for document bytes and integrity metadata. | Short-lived server-authorized retrieval only; no public bucket. | Confirmed
Async | Queue and worker for import processing, notifications, projection, retention candidates. | Idempotent handler, explicit retry and dead-letter/review path. | Proposal
2 Routes and Server Boundaries
Route family | Examples | Server rule | Cache and response | Status
Public | /; /directory; /exam-centres; /public/status | Use release-gated projection only; never query private operational tables directly. | CDN only for approved projection; cache tags/versioning; no identity keys. | Needs Legal Review
Authentication | /api/auth/* | Auth.js handlers only; callback and session settings from environment. | No-store; avoid account enumeration. | Confirmed
Private UI | /app/*; /admin/* | Page loader performs server session/policy check before data query. | Private/no-store by default; 403 or safe not-found. | Confirmed
Protected mutation | Server Actions and /api/* route handlers | Resolve action, role grant, geo/org scope, target and workflow state inside server module. | No-store; atomic transaction; audit before success response. | Confirmed
Objects and export | /api/documents/*; /api/exports/* | Authorize every retrieval/creation; issue short-lived object reference only after policy check. | No CDN for private bytes; download/export rate and volume controls. | Proposal
Operational | /health/ready; /health/live; /internal/jobs/* | Readiness has no secrets; internal jobs require machine identity and allow-listed network/control. | No-store; minimal response. | Proposal

3 Authentication Authorization and Transactions
Auth.js establishes identity; it does not by itself grant domain access. A protected operation resolves the actor’s current grant from PostgreSQL and applies the RBAC and geographic/organisation scope model. The server ignores client-supplied role, action, scope and target ownership claims.

Concern | Architecture rule | Implementation boundary | Status
Session | Authenticate request and check account state on protected entry points. | Server components, Server Actions and route handlers. | Confirmed
Authorization | Resolve action + role + active grant + geo/org scope + target + workflow; insufficient result is 403. | Server-only policy module and scope-filtered Prisma queries. | Confirmed
Protected write | Write domain change, immutable status/decision event, audit and outbox record in one PostgreSQL transaction. | Prisma interactive transaction with bounded duration. | Confirmed
Correction | Create a later correction/revocation event rather than changing prior historical fact. | Event append service; current-state view/query. | Confirmed
Async handoff | Publish from durable outbox after commit; worker de-duplicates by message key. | Queue adapter and idempotent job handler. | Proposal
Maker-checker | Reject same maker/checker for configured decision classes; checker repeats scope and policy check. | Decision service and unique/check constraints where feasible. | Proposal
4 Data Storage and Migration Strategy
Area | Design | Operational control | Status
PostgreSQL | Normalized tables in the ERD; UUID keys; FK/unique/check/index constraints; event-derived status. | Migration reviewed, versioned and applied through controlled deployment. | Proposal
Prisma | Schema maps the approved logical model. Transactions retain database constraints as final authority. | No schema push from developer runtime to production. | Proposal
Object storage | Private bytes; document_record stores storage key, integrity reference and minimal metadata. | Server checks scope/action before signed retrieval; scan/quarantine path for imports. | Confirmed
Cache | Public projection may use explicit cache invalidation/tag/version after approved release. Private reads remain no-store. | Do not cache authorization decisions or highly restricted rows at edge. | Confirmed
Search/read models | Create separate, release-gated projection for public directories; operational source tables remain private. | Projection build is queued, versioned and auditable. | Needs Legal Review
Retention | Store policy reference/disposition event, not hard-coded official periods. | DPO/legal/owner decision required before real-data retention or disposal automation. | Needs Legal Review
5 Queue Jobs and Rate Limits
Area | Design requirement | Failure and recovery | Status
Import jobs | Upload private object then create import_job; worker validates template and rows without promoting until checker rule is met. | Quarantine invalid/suspected real data; retry safe step or send to review queue. | Proposal
Projection jobs | Build public projection from approved source and release decision, never from client request. | Keep prior approved projection; publish only an atomic version switch. | Needs Legal Review
Notifications | Use outbox and idempotency key; notification is side effect after committed decision. | Retry with backoff; dead-letter for review; never reverse domain event automatically. | Proposal
Rate limit | Apply edge limits for public requests and tighter identity/action/scope-aware limits for login, object, export and mutation routes. | Return 429 with safe retry guidance; monitor repeated denials. | Proposal
Worker trust | Jobs carry opaque target IDs, not trusted authorization claims. Worker reloads current policy/state before side effect. | Reject stale/invalid job; audit disposition. | Confirmed

6 Audit Monitoring Backup and Environments
Area | Baseline | Recovery evidence | Status
Audit | Append audit_event for protected reads/mutations/denials where permitted; redact sensitive values. | Correlate request, actor, action, scope outcome, target reference and result. | Confirmed
Monitoring | Metrics for latency, error rate, queue depth, job failures, authorization denials, database connection health and backup status. | Alert on thresholds; runbook links to containment and recovery actions. | Proposal
Logs | Structured server/worker logs with request and job correlation IDs; no secrets or raw private fields. | Restrict access; retain/dispose under approved policy. | Needs Legal Review
Backup | Encrypted PostgreSQL backups and object inventory/version protection; independently controlled backup credentials. | Scheduled restore verification in non-production once approved; document RPO/RTO target. | Proposal
Environments | local synthetic-only, test synthetic-only, staging synthetic-only, production gated for real data only after readiness decision. | Separate databases/buckets/queue namespaces and credentials. | Confirmed
Secrets | Environment-injected secrets; no secret in repository, browser bundle, seed, fixture or log. | Rotate/revoke after exposure; audit deployment/config access. | Confirmed
Environment Variables
Group | Examples of names only | Rule | Status
Identity | AUTH_SECRET; AUTH_URL; AUTH_PROVIDER_* | Server-only; rotate through approved secret process. | Confirmed
Database | DATABASE_URL; DIRECT_DATABASE_URL | Server-only; least-privilege runtime and migration credentials are separate. | Proposal
Objects | OBJECT_STORAGE_ENDPOINT; OBJECT_STORAGE_BUCKET; OBJECT_STORAGE_* | Private endpoint/credentials only; never prefixed for browser exposure. | Confirmed
Queue and observability | QUEUE_URL; OTEL_EXPORTER_*; ERROR_REPORTING_DSN | Separate per environment; redact payloads. | Proposal
Edge | WAF_POLICY_ID; RATE_LIMIT_*; CDN_REVALIDATE_SECRET | Configuration reviewed; invalidate/revoke on incident. | Proposal
7 Failure Modes and Recovery
Failure mode | Containment | Recovery | Status
Authorization service/scope ambiguity | Fail closed: 403 with no private/existence disclosure; no mutation. | Restore scope/policy data; retry with fresh server decision; review denied/audit signals. | Confirmed
Transaction/event/audit/outbox failure | Rollback all related protected writes. | Reconcile only committed latest state; do not manually overwrite history. | Confirmed
Queue outage or poison job | Retain outbox/job state; pause side effect and do not lose committed domain record. | Retry idempotently with bounded backoff; dead-letter and review. | Proposal
Database outage | Readiness fails; reject protected writes; preserve consistency. | Restore service/replica/backup under runbook; validate before reopening. | Proposal
Object store outage | Block upload/download confirmation; no fallback public bucket. | Retry safely; preserve document metadata as pending only where transaction design permits. | Confirmed
WAF or rate-limit false positive | Return safe 403/429; preserve request correlation. | Review rule/rate configuration with change control; roll back rule if approved. | Proposal
Suspected real data in synthetic route | Quarantine object/import/log pathway; block release and export. | Notify owner/DPO/legal reviewer; do not claim compliance outcome. | Needs Legal Review
8 Architecture Decision Records
ADR | Decision | Reason and consequence | Status
ADR 01 | Adopt modular monolith, not microservices. | Single governed codebase lowers early operational complexity; domain modules retain clear boundaries. Reassess only with measured scaling/ownership evidence. | Confirmed
ADR 02 | Use server-side policy authorization for every protected read/write. | Client/UI is not a security boundary. Scope-filtered queries and safe 403 are mandatory. | Confirmed
ADR 03 | Use PostgreSQL event history and derived current state. | Status, grant, review and audit corrections append events; earlier records are not overwritten. | Confirmed
ADR 04 | Keep document bytes in private object storage. | Database stores metadata/integrity/explicit links only; retrieval is separately authorized. | Confirmed
ADR 05 | Use transactional outbox and idempotent workers. | Avoid side effects before commit and support retry without duplicate notification/projection. | Proposal
ADR 06 | Use separate public projection and release gate. | Avoid accidental exposure from operational tables; release authority and content require review. | Needs Legal Review
ADR 07 | Keep real data out until readiness gate. | Synthetic-only environments/seeds/logs enable design work without asserting authorization for real-data processing. | Confirmed
9 Architecture Review Checklist
Review item | Evidence requested | Status
Route boundaries | Confirm public projection routes, private route families and internal health/job exposure. | Proposal
Policy contract | Confirm action codes, scope inheritance and maker-checker decision classes. | Proposal
Operations | Set SLOs, RPO/RTO, backup restore cadence, on-call/runbooks and alert thresholds. | Proposal
Legal/governance | Approve real-data readiness, retention/disposal, public release and official authority evidence. | Needs Legal Review
Implementation review | Review migrations, server guards, object authorization, queue idempotency and negative cross-scope=403 tests after build. | Proposal

documents.label: MIGRATION STRATEGY
documents.text:
# Prisma migration strategy

## Status labels

- **Confirmed** — PostgreSQL + Prisma; production uses a direct migration connection distinct from the pooled runtime connection. Changes follow `expand → migrate/backfill → contract` and protected mutations write domain/event/audit/outbox atomically.
- **Proposal** — generate the baseline with `prisma migrate dev --create-only --schema prisma/schema.prisma --name init`, then append the reviewed contents of `prisma/sql/integrity_guards.sql` to that generated migration before review. Do not hand-run `db push` in production.
- **Needs Legal Review** — real-data import, retention disposition, public projection release, and legal evidence become executable only after DPO/nิติกร review and evidence approval. This repository carries no real legal source or personal data.

## Migration procedure

1. **Expand:** add nullable columns/new tables/new indexes only; generate migration from the canonical schema.
2. **Validate:** run fresh and upgrade tests against an isolated synthetic PostgreSQL database; inspect generated SQL and lock impact.
3. **Backfill:** run an idempotent, resumable job recorded in `ImportJob`/`OutboxEvent`; emit audit evidence. Do not overwrite historic events.
4. **Contract:** only after observability confirms no old reader/writer remains, remove obsolete paths in a later migration.

## Failure and recovery

- Migration failure: stop deployment, preserve logs/change record, roll back the compatible application release if required, then apply a reviewed **forward fix**. Do not issue destructive automatic down migrations.
- Lock/timeout: stop rollout, assess lock owner and retry window; split index creation or use PostgreSQL online-index approach when approved.
- Bad backfill: stop job, retain source and row errors, append compensating domain/status events and replay idempotently; restore from approved backup only under the change record.
- Secret exposure: revoke/rotate the credential, invalidate the run, and rerun on a clean synthetic environment.

## Required test modes

- `fresh`: empty database receives every migration and integrity guard.
- `upgrade`: fixture at the immediately previous released migration upgrades without data loss; append-only rows remain unchanged.
- `forward-fix`: a deliberately failed compatible migration is remediated by a new additive migration; no history is deleted or rewritten.

`tests/migration/run-migration-tests.sh` first derives an SQL plan with `prisma migrate diff`, then applies it to three separately provisioned isolated PostgreSQL databases. CI must provide the exact previous released datamodel plus synthetic upgrade/forward-fix assertion SQL; the runner refuses to invent history or create/drop a database. Run it only with `FRESH_DATABASE_URL`, `UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL`, `FORWARD_FIX_DATABASE_URL`, and `ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_MIGRATION_TESTS=true`.

# Deterministic synthetic seed

## Status labels

- **Confirmed** — the seed creates fictional `SYN-*` records only; it requires a local `*_dev`, `*_test`, or `*synthetic` PostgreSQL URL plus `ALLOW_SYNTHETIC_SEED=true`. It neither deletes data nor updates append-only events, audit records, document versions, or outbox rows.
- **Proposal** — CI provisions a disposable database, runs `tsx prisma/seed.ts` twice, and runs `tsx tests/seed/stable-rerun.ts`; counts after first and second run must match.
- **Needs Legal Review** — no real person, legal source, personal identifier, retention disposition, or production target may be introduced through this seed.

## Coverage

The deterministic namespace creates an organisation/scope hierarchy, education unit, examination centre, two fictional persons, acting → ended and appointed → ended position history, organisation/application status events, a candidate/application, a synthetic document reference, audit events, and outbox events.

## Failure and recovery

- Guard failure: the seed stops before any write when the target is not an approved local synthetic database. Correct the test environment; never bypass the guard for production.
- Transaction failure: PostgreSQL rolls back the seed transaction. Fix the failing synthetic fixture and rerun; deterministic primary keys and `skipDuplicates` make recovery safe.
- Count mismatch: stop CI, inspect only synthetic records under the fixed namespace, and add a forward correction. Do not delete or overwrite historical event/audit/outbox rows.

# Audit and approval

- **Confirmed:** Change requests are server-authorized and include a privacy-safe diff. A different maker/checker is enforced server-side. Audit events append create, update, approve, reject, import, export and auth-risk actions with actor, target, request, outcome and time.
- **Proposal:** The hash chain is an application-level tamper-evidence control; production must also use immutable database/object retention and independent monitoring.
- **Needs Legal Review:** Audit retention, reviewer authority, export log visibility, legal hold and incident disclosure requirements need owner/DPO/legal review. No compliance determination is made.

Failure/recovery: invalid or self review fails before write; a transaction failure restores the request/audit/outbox set. Audit records do not retain secrets, tokens, raw payloads or unnecessary PII. Corrections append a later event; do not alter earlier audit history. Hash-chain verification detects tampering and must trigger investigation using immutable storage copies.

# Auth and server authorization

- **Confirmed:** Auth.js/Next.js resolves session on the server; policy is deny-by-default and evaluates actor, active grant, action, trusted resource scope, workflow/maker-checker and session expiry. UI never grants access.
- **Proposal:** admin and security-reviewer roles require enrolled MFA before a session is created. Session cookie options and identity-provider configuration must be set only through environment-injected secrets.
- **Needs Legal Review:** production identity proofing, MFA recovery/retention, real user account lifecycle and access-log retention require DPO/nิติกร evidence review.

Failure/recovery: expired or missing session returns safe 401; all authorization failures return safe 403 without resource enumeration; MFA recovery revokes existing sessions and requires a separately approved recovery workflow. A transaction error rolls back business/history/audit/outbox together; retry only with an idempotency key.

documents.text:
# Private documents

- **Confirmed:** Object bytes use private storage only; public buckets are rejected. Server authorization precedes upload, scan recording and signed-download issuance. Metadata stores object key, MIME, size, checksum and retention; document versions, events, audit and outbox are append-only.
- **Proposal:** MIME allowlist, size limit, signed-URL TTL and storage scan adapter are deployment configuration. Scan worker retries/dead-letter handling must be provided by the approved queue platform.
- **Needs Legal Review:** Retention/disposal period, legal hold, document classification, scanner evidence, upload/download authority, recovery, and real-document release rules need owner/DPO/legal review. No compliance determination is made.

Failure/recovery: policy failure rejects before metadata write; malware produces a quarantine event and blocks signed download; expired URLs fail closed. A new clean object is a new document version; do not replace the quarantined or prior version. If scan infrastructure fails, retain `PENDING`, block download and retry through the queue rather than promoting the object.

# Go-live, handover and PIR runbook — synthetic baseline

## Status labels

**Confirmed**

- The handover pack checker validates eight existing runbook assets, five named role responsibilities, staged-rollout definitions, daily-review and 7/30-day PIR templates.
- All templates request aggregates and safe evidence only; server authorization and append-only history remain required.
- A complete file pack is not a real go-live, owner decision or support acknowledgement.

**Proposal**

- Run daily early reviews for the owner-approved early-life period; this baseline supplies day templates, not a scheduled operational commitment.
- Owner approves rollout scope, pilot population, rollout/freeze thresholds, KPI targets and PIR dates before any production use.

**Needs Legal Review**

- Support records, KPI retention, incident/PIR distribution, change-freeze authority, data correction authority and any production-data processing require owner/DPO/legal review. No policy period or law is inferred.

## Ownership and handover

| Role | Owns |
|---|---|
| Service Owner | Go/no-go, exceptions and 7/30-day PIR decision. |
| Release Owner | Artifact, rollout/freeze/rollback evidence. |
| Support Lead | Daily review, support intake, escalation and acknowledgement. |
| Security/Privacy Owner | Authorization/privacy incident path and evidence access. |
| Data Owner | Data-quality KPIs, corrections, reconciliation and retention decisions. |

Required handover pack: release, backup/restore, monitoring, UAT, QA, legacy migration, training/SOP and audit/approval runbooks. Record owner/support acknowledgement separately; a blank acknowledgement remains `PENDING_OWNER_SUPPORT_ACK`.

## Staged rollout and freeze

| Stage | Entry gate | Action | Freeze / recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prepare | Approved artifact, backup/restore, migration/UAT/support evidence. | Keep flags off. | Any missing evidence: no-go. |
| Pilot | Approved limited scope and smoke/monitoring evidence. | Enable one reversible flag. | Hold/disable flag for anomaly. |
| Hold | Daily review has no unresolved blocker. | Do not expand. | Freeze on incident, reconciliation or evidence gap. |
| Expand | Owner accepts pilot and support readiness. | Increase approved scope only. | Route back to prior artifact/flags; no history deletion. |
| Steady state | 7-day review accepted. | Operations owns runbooks and KPIs. | Continue rollback/freeze if new blocker appears. |

Freeze criteria: failed smoke or restore evidence; UAT/sign-off gap; unauthorized/privacy concern; failed migration/reconciliation; monitoring/queue/scan/backup alarm; missing support owner; or a condition declared by the owner’s approved SLO. Recovery is stop expansion, hold flags, use the release rollback plan, preserve minimum evidence and obtain a new decision.

## Daily early review

For each approved review day, record: rollout scope/flag state; smoke and monitoring signals (error, latency, DB, auth, rate limit, queue/DLQ, scan, backup); incidents; data quality/reconciliation/backlog KPI aggregates; support/training gaps; freeze/rollback decision and safe evidence references. Do not attach raw payload, secrets or protected content.

## 7- and 30-day PIR

| Review | Required output |
|---|---|
| Day 7 PIR | Rollout evidence, early KPI trend, incidents/changes, data-quality findings, backlog, runbook/training updates, owner decision. |
| Day 30 PIR | Sustained KPI trend, recurrent issues/root causes, data correction/reconciliation, security/privacy findings, backlog prioritization, operating-model and improvement decision. |

Both PIRs remain `PENDING_OWNER_REVIEW` until an owner records the decision and evidence.

## Backlog and data-quality KPI definitions

| KPI | Use |
|---|---|
| Open backlog / reopened requests | Workload, age and recurrence by safe category/status. |
| Validation rejection rate | Input/process quality; trend by entity/area without payload. |
| Quarantined duplicate count | Dedupe pressure and canonical-record review workload. |
| Reconciliation variance | Migration/import consistency by entity/status/area. |
| Correction request rate | Append-only correction volume and effective-date conflict trend. |

Targets, warning bands and owner actions are intentionally unset until approved baseline measurements exist.

## Current execution boundary

`npm run test:golive:handover` proves that the synthetic handover pack, templates and role definitions are internally complete. It does not prove production deployment, support staffing, backup/restore, monitoring integration, UAT sign-off, production KPI measurement, owner acknowledgement or go-live. Current production decision remains **NO-GO**.

# Import commit reliability

- **Confirmed:** Commit is server-authorized before a batch transaction. The transaction writes the batch, imported staging records, batch event, audit, outbox and idempotency receipt together, or restores the full write set. A completed idempotency key returns its original result without duplicate records.
- **Proposal:** A commit promotes validated synthetic rows to an import staging record, not directly to production domain entities. The client must supply one idempotency key per logical delivery; production storage must enforce its uniqueness.
- **Needs Legal Review:** Authority to commit, retention of import/audit evidence, compensation approval, source-file retention and any promotion of real account-form data require owner/DPO/legal review. No compliance determination is made.

Failure/recovery: a crash inside the transaction rolls back batch, records, audit, outbox and receipt, so the same delivery can retry safely. A duplicate delivery returns the stored result. Row errors block the whole batch before a write. After a successful commit, use a forward-only compensation request; never delete or overwrite the original batch/history.

# Legacy migration runbook — synthetic baseline

## Controls and status labels

**Confirmed**

- The baseline has a pure synthetic dry-run service: it reports `dbWrites: 0`, inventories source records, maps/cleanses them, quarantines duplicates, reconciles counts and verifies samples.
- Approval requires an actor different from the submitting maker when the resource is marked `requiresIndependentApprover`.
- Cutover and rollback append migration/audit evidence in the synthetic model. Rollback never deletes source records, target history or audit evidence.

**Proposal**

- Use the stated thresholds for a migration run only after the data owner approves the entity/status/area definitions and the exception policy.
- Create immutable source snapshots/checksums, restrict source to read-only, and retain source until the owner-approved retention period expires.
- Perform production cutover only after a separately approved staging rehearsal, reconciliation report and explicit owner decision.

**Needs Legal Review**

- Source/target retention length, lawful authority to use legacy identifiers, data-subject handling, official form mapping, deletion approval, and signatory authority require DPO/legal/owner review. No law, person or policy period is inferred here.

## Migration path and gates

| Stage | Input / action | Required evidence | Block / recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Inventory | Read-only synthetic source manifest with source ID, entity, status, area, version and synthetic flag. | Total plus counts by entity/status/area; source snapshot reference. | Invalid/missing fields: block mapping; correct source copy without changing the original. |
| 2. Field mapping | Versioned map `legacy entity → target table/entity`; map only confirmed fields. | Mapping version, owner reviewer, unmapped-field report. | Unknown field: quarantine as `UNMAPPED_ENTITY`; do not guess. |
| 3. Cleanse | Trim/canonicalize synthetic IDs/status/area, preserving source ID/version. | Cleanse log and exceptions. | Required value absent: row error; correct a new staging copy and rerun. |
| 4. Dedupe | Match synthetic entity + dedupe key; retain one canonical target candidate and quarantine the duplicate. | Canonical/duplicate source IDs and rationale. | Ambiguous match: quarantine; require owner review, never auto-merge history. |
| 5. Dry-run | Execute map/cleanse/dedupe/reconciliation with `dbWrites: 0`. | Zero-write result, row errors, accepted/quarantined counts. | Any write or parser error: invalidate run, preserve evidence, fix and rerun. |
| 6. Reconcile | Compare accepted target candidates to expected counts by entity/status/area; verify named samples. | Count report, variance, samples, exception register. | Threshold fail: block approval/cutover; resolve exception or obtain documented waiver. |
| 7. Approve | Independent server-authorized approver reviews threshold result and source retention confirmation. | Approval ID, actor role, scope, timestamp, evidence bundle. | Same maker/checker or expired scope: 403; assign a valid independent approver. |
| 8. Cutover | Activate the approved synthetic batch only. | Build/run ID, accepted count, audit/outbox records, post-cutover reconciliation. | Abort before activation if any gate fails; retain source untouched. |
| 9. Rollback | Disable/route away from cutover and append rollback/compensation evidence. | Reason, timestamp, preserved-record count, audit record. | Never delete source or historical target rows; forward-fix after investigation. |

## Synthetic mapping and threshold profile

| Item | Synthetic value |
|---|---|
| Source inventory | 10 source records; entities PERSON, ORGANIZATION, POSITION, EDUCATION_UNIT, APPLICATION |
| Dedupe scenario | 1 known PERSON duplicate is quarantined; 9 accepted target candidates remain |
| Count dimensions | `entity + status + area`; source totals remain visible, target totals count accepted candidates only |
| Sample verification | 3 named synthetic source→target mappings must all pass |
| Thresholds exercised | count variance = 0; invalid rows ≤ 0; quarantined duplicates ≤ 1; all samples pass; source retention confirmed before approval |
| Source retention | `RETAINED_PENDING_POLICY` during dry-run, then `RETAINED_CONFIRMED` before approval/cutover. No delete operation exists. |

## Current execution boundary

`npm run test:migration:legacy` executes an in-memory synthetic migration rehearsal. It is not a legacy-source inventory, production dry-run, PostgreSQL migration, data-owner approval, staging cutover or legal retention decision. Its synthetic `APPROVED_SYNTHETIC` record demonstrates server-side separation of maker/checker only; it is not a real authorization or sign-off.

# Monitoring and incident runbook — synthetic baseline

## Status labels

**Confirmed**

- The observability helper defines eight required metrics and allowlists safe log/trace attributes.
- Sensitive-shaped fields (for example payload, body, token, authorization, email and contact fields) are excluded from the helper output.
- The local alert drill evaluates all eight synthetic rules and stores incident updates as append-only events.

**Proposal**

- Connect the metric names and structured events to the approved metrics/logs/traces back end; use dashboard and alert-route references controlled by the owner.
- Synthetic thresholds below are starting points only. The service owner must approve production SLOs, windows, severity mappings and escalation recipients.
- Propagate a generated request/correlation ID across web, API, queue/job, database audit and object-scan events; store only pseudonymous/approved dimensions.

**Needs Legal Review**

- Log/trace retention, incident evidence retention, access to observability data, external notification, and postmortem distribution require owner/DPO/legal review. No compliance or retention period is asserted.

## Metrics, telemetry and proposed alerts

| Signal | Metric / safe dimensions | Proposed drill condition | Initial response |
|---|---|---|---|
| Error rate | `http_request_error_ratio`; route template/status class/area code | ≥ 0.05 | Stop rollout; inspect safe traces/logs. |
| Latency | `http_request_duration_p95_ms`; route template/area code | ≥ 1000 ms | Inspect dependency/query latency. |
| Database | `db_connection_saturation_ratio`; DB role | ≥ 0.85 | Protect DB; pause non-critical jobs. |
| Authorization | `auth_denial_total`; reason code/area code | ≥ 20 | Investigate policy regression or abuse; never log credentials. |
| Rate limit | `rate_limit_rejection_total`; route template | ≥ 50 | Inspect traffic/WAF/rate-limit policy. |
| Dead letter queue | `queue_dead_letter_depth`; queue name | ≥ 1 | Pause unsafe consumer; diagnose/replay idempotently. |
| Object scan | `document_scan_failure_total`; reason code | ≥ 1 | Quarantine object; keep access denied. |
| Backup | `backup_verification_state`; backup class | verification false | Release no-go; investigate restore evidence. |

Thresholds are **Proposal**, expressed only for the synthetic drill. They are not measured production baselines or approved SLOs.

## Logging and tracing contract

Allowed logs/traces contain only: timestamp, level, event, request/trace ID, route template, method, status code, duration, area code, actor pseudonym, error code, component and count. Use error codes and correlation IDs instead of a raw request/response, SQL value, object name, document metadata, authorization header, session, contact value or user identifier.

Logs are operational telemetry, not a replacement for append-only audit. Audit continues to record the minimum authorized change evidence; monitoring links through correlation IDs.

## Alert drill and incident handling

1. Inject the synthetic observations in `tests/observability/alert-drill.test.mjs`; do not send a live alert from this baseline.
2. Verify all expected alert rule IDs, severity and safe response appear.
3. Open an append-only incident event with the alert IDs and correlation ID; hold release flags where appropriate.
4. Validate escalation ownership from the approved on-call roster—this repository stores no personal roster.
5. Create a postmortem record with impact, timeline, root cause, recovery, follow-up and evidence-retention review. It begins `PENDING_OWNER_REVIEW`.

| Severity | Trigger examples | Escalation / recovery |
|---|---|---|
| SEV1 | Backup verification absent; confirmed critical availability/security-control impact. | Incident commander + security/release owner; stop rollout, protect data, preserve minimal evidence. |
| SEV2 | Error/DB/auth spike, DLQ or scan failure affecting a critical workflow. | Service owner + on-call; isolate queue/upload/feature, use idempotent retry or rollback plan. |
| SEV3 | Latency/rate-limit deterioration without confirmed critical loss. | Service owner during approved response window; diagnose and tune with change control. |
| SEV4 | Informational anomaly. | Record/triage; promote only if impact changes. |

## Failure modes and recovery

- Telemetry backend unavailable: fail safely without blocking authorized business transaction unless policy requires; buffer only non-sensitive bounded telemetry, drop safely on limit and expose a health metric.
- Alert route unavailable: record delivery failure, page via approved alternate process and do not mark drill complete.
- DLQ/scan failure: quarantine and preserve minimal audit; no automatic unsafe replay or document release.
- Backup alert: no-go for release; create new evidence and run isolated restore verification.
- Monitoring data suggests privacy leakage: restrict access, stop offending export, preserve minimal forensic reference, rotate/revoke only under approved incident procedure.

## Current execution boundary

`npm run test:monitoring:drill` is an in-memory synthetic alert drill. No real metrics backend, trace exporter, alert delivery, pager escalation, production dashboard, DB telemetry, queue, scan service or backup system was contacted. It is therefore not evidence of operational alert delivery or incident response readiness.

# Full QA Matrix — synthetic baseline

## Status rules

**Confirmed**

- The runnable rows below map a synthetic requirement to an executable Node test in this baseline.
- `test:qa:coverage` emits `PASS` only after the mapped command exits `0`; its console output is the execution evidence for that run.
- Authorization is evaluated on the server in the mapped negative-access test. UI visibility is not accepted as authorization evidence.
- Existing historical/event tests use append-only records; they are not an authorization to overwrite history.

- CI retains the QA command output as a build artifact and blocks promotion on a runnable-row failure or an evidence-less claimed pass.
- Browser accessibility and responsive viewport checks should be added to the same runner after agreed route/viewport/browser coverage is available.

**Needs Legal Review**

# Production release runbook — synthetic rehearsal baseline

## Status labels

**Confirmed**

- `test:release:rehearsal` checks a synthetic release gate, executes three local smoke regressions, and produces a non-destructive rollback plan.
- The gate refuses non-synthetic data/run types and always returns `NO_GO_PRODUCTION`.
- The CI workflow below runs release rehearsal only; it has no cloud credentials, deployment, migration, feature-flag or production-write step.

**Proposal**

- Production release follows: approved immutable artifact → verified backup/restore point → backward-compatible migration → deploy → smoke → incremental feature flags → cache/search rebuild → monitored handoff.
- Release owner defines the SLO thresholds, alert routes, freeze window and approval identities before any real production use.

**Needs Legal Review**

- Production-data authority, retention/deletion, approver/signatory authority, incident communication, export impact and audit-evidence retention require owner/DPO/legal review. No law or retention duration is assumed.

## Go / no-go gate

| Gate | Evidence required | No-go / recovery |
|---|---|---|
| Immutable artifact | Commit/build ID and immutable artifact digest; prior known-good digest. | Missing/mutable artifact: do not deploy; rebuild through CI. |
| Backup and restore | New recovery-point reference plus isolated restore evidence. | Missing/failed evidence: no-go; create/verify a new backup. Do not trust backup without restore evidence. |
| Migration | Approved, backward-compatible plan; schema-old/new job compatibility; source retention maintained. | Failed/unknown migration: no-go; restore traffic to prior artifact and use approved forward-fix—no untracked down migration. |
| Feature flags | All release flags initially off; owner for each flag and rollback behavior recorded. | Flag not controllable: no-go; disable/remove from release scope. |
| Deploy | Environment-specific credentials and immutable artifact match recorded; server authorization remains enabled. | Artifact/config mismatch: stop rollout; retain evidence; redeploy known-good artifact only. |
| Smoke | Health, authorized mutation, cross-scope 403, public privacy projection and critical synthetic migration checks pass with evidence. | Any failure: stop flags/rollout, preserve logs without excess PII, invoke rollback plan. |
| Cache/search rebuild | Job ID, input version, count/reconciliation and completion state recorded. | Failed/partial rebuild: keep stale-safe behavior or disable affected feature; rerun idempotently after diagnosis. |
| Monitoring | Dashboard and alert-route references; error, latency, queue/job, auth denial, DB health and backup signals visible. | Missing signal/alert route: no-go; restore observability before rollout. |

## Release sequence

1. Freeze the approved artifact and configuration diff; obtain release-owner approval.
2. Create a recovery point and verify an isolated restore. Record both references.
3. Run only backward-compatible approved migrations from CI; keep old/new readers and jobs compatible.
4. Set release feature flags off. Deploy the immutable artifact using environment-specific credentials.
5. Run smoke checks; record command/output/correlation IDs. Do not treat UI visibility as authorization evidence.
6. Enable one approved flag at a time and observe the agreed monitoring window. Rebuild cache/search through idempotent jobs; reconcile counts.
7. Record monitoring handoff and final go/no-go. Contract migrations and source deletion are later, separately approved work.

## Rollback criteria and recovery

Rollback/stop-rollout criteria are: failed smoke, failed authorization/privacy check, failed migration/reconciliation, monitoring breach under the owner-approved SLO, unsafe queue/job behavior, or unavailable backup/restore evidence.

1. Set release flags off and stop further rollout.
2. Route to the prior immutable artifact; keep backward-compatible schema in place.
3. Do not delete source, history or audit. Use an approved forward-fix/compensation for data issues.
4. Preserve minimal incident/audit evidence; rebuild cache/search only after consistency is understood.
5. Re-run smoke and obtain a new owner decision before any re-release.

## Reproducible CI/CD boundary

`.github/workflows/release-rehearsal.yml` pins the Node version and runs the release rehearsal, QA coverage, migration rehearsal and UAT-script check. It intentionally cannot perform a production deployment. A real production pipeline must additionally use protected environments, independent approvals, immutable artifacts, isolated credentials and evidence retention approved by the owner.

## Current execution boundary

This repository has no completed production backup, restore, migration, deploy, cache/search rebuild, monitoring handoff, UAT owner sign-off or release approval. Therefore the only valid current production decision is **NO-GO**. `SMOKE_AND_ROLLBACK_READY_SYNTHETIC` means the local rehearsal passed, not that production is ready.

# Threat model

| Threat | Severity | Prevent | Detect | Respond | Test | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Auth bypass | High | Server session/MFA | 401/403 audit | Revoke sessions | Negative session test | OPEN — evidence required |
| IDOR/BOLA | High | Server scope checks | 403/audit | Revoke grant | Cross-scope test | OPEN — evidence required |
| XSS | High | Encoding/CSP | CSP reports | Disable/patch | XSS test | OPEN — evidence required |
| CSRF | High | SameSite/origin token | Rejections | Invalidate session | Cross-origin test | OPEN — evidence required |
| SQLi | High | Parameterized ORM/validation | Anomaly alerts | Block/rotate | Injection test | OPEN — evidence required |
| File upload | High | Private scan/quarantine | Scan events | Keep blocked | Malware/expiry test | OPEN — evidence required |
| Mass assignment | High | DTO allow-list | Unexpected fields | Reject/review | Forbidden-field test | OPEN — evidence required |
| Escalation | High | Deny default/maker-checker | Grant audit | Revoke/review | Self-approval/403 | OPEN — evidence required |
| Leakage | High | Public projection/private objects | Privacy audit | Withdraw release | Projection privacy | OPEN — evidence required |
| DDoS | High | WAF/rate/backpressure | 429/latency | Throttle/scale | Load test | OPEN — evidence required |
| Secrets | High | Secret manager/redaction | Secret scan | Rotate/revoke | CI scan | OPEN — evidence required |
| Supply chain | High | Lockfile/pinned CI | SCA alerts | Pin/forward fix | SCA CI | OPEN — evidence required |

- **Confirmed:** Server-side authorization, append-only audit, public projection, private documents, rate limiting and import controls are architecture controls; UI is not a security boundary.
- **Proposal:** CSP details, CSRF pattern, WAF thresholds, SCA tooling and incident runbooks require implementation approval.
- **Needs Legal Review:** Breach notification, retention, real-data incident handling and disclosure require owner/DPO/legal review. No compliance determination is made.

Failure/recovery: security control failure must fail closed, create a minimal auth-risk audit event, preserve evidence without secrets/PII, and use revocation/forward-fix rather than overwriting history. No Critical/High item is marked resolved without executed evidence.

documents.label: TRAINING SOP
documents.text:
# Training and SOP — synthetic baseline

## Status labels

**Confirmed**

- Five role SOPs and seven `TRAIN-*` exercises are defined in the training registry.
- Every exercise requires server-side authorization, safe evidence and append-only correction/audit behavior.
- The exercise checker validates the pack and its related regression scripts; it never certifies a human trainee.

**Proposal**

- Assign a trainer, training environment, duration, assessment threshold and retraining cycle through the owner’s approved learning process.
- Store each trainee’s evidence by exercise ID and have a trainer sign the record only after observing the exercise in an approved environment.

**Needs Legal Review**

- Training-record retention, use of screenshots, access to protected training views, trainer authority and handling of suspected real data require owner/DPO/legal review. This SOP makes no compliance claim.

## Non-negotiable common rules

1. Use only `TRAIN-*` synthetic fixtures. If a real/suspected real record appears, stop, do not copy it, restrict/quarantine access and notify the owner/DPO/legal route.
2. UI visibility is not permission. Every protected read/write/approval/import/export is authorized by the server for actor, action, resource and scope.
3. Never put password, MFA code, token, authorization header, raw protected payload, contact value or document content in a training note, chat, log or screenshot.
4. Correct data by appending a dated event/version or approved change request. Never overwrite historical appointment, status, application, import or audit history.
5. Preserve safe evidence: exercise ID, fixture ID, date/environment, trainer, result/correlation ID and safe error code. Do not record excess personal data.

## Role SOPs

| Role | Standard workflow | Privacy / approval rule | Error recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Data Entry | Search duplicate; enter confirmed synthetic core fields; choose visibility; submit. | Minimum fields; reviewer approves change. | Validation/duplicate: correct staged input or canonical link; do not overwrite. |
| Registrar | Create candidate; submit core-only or approved-mapped application in window; check status event. | Restricted views only; mapping exception goes to reviewer. | Duplicate/window: retain snapshot and append permitted action/status later. |
| Reviewer | Inspect diff/effective date/evidence; approve or reject. | Independent from maker; no unnecessary export/payload access. | Reject safely and return to maker for append-only correction. |
| Admin | Manage synthetic scope/role grants; test session/MFA/deny behavior. | No self-elevation/direct untracked business change. | 401 reauthenticate; 403 request authorized scope—never bypass. |
| Auditor | Trace correlation across change/import/auth events; inspect audit completeness. | Minimal metadata only; read-only independent finding. | Suspected real/sensitive data: stop, restrict and report via approved route. |

## Import, error recovery and data correction SOP

| Situation | Required response |
|---|---|
| Import file error | Upload synthetic versioned template; dry-run first; read row/column/code/message/fix; confirm zero DB writes; correct source copy and rerun. |
| Approved import commit | Only independent authorized approver may release clean preview; use idempotency key; retain import/audit receipt. |
| Duplicate | Do not merge/delete on guess. Preserve candidate/history; submit canonical/exception review. |
| Validation error | Correct unsaved input; for saved business state append approved correction event. |
| Permission/session error | Stop. Reauthenticate for 401 or request scope for 403; no client/UI workaround. |
| Incorrect historical data | Record a new dated correction/change request with reason and approval; retain earlier entry/audit. |
| Job/scan/import failure | Quarantine unsafe item; preserve minimal evidence; use approved retry, idempotent replay or forward compensation only. |

## Role exercises and pass evidence

| Exercise | Role | Synthetic objective | Evidence trainer reviews |
|---|---|---|---|
| EX-DATA-01 | Data Entry | Core entry/visibility validation | Safe correlation/result and validation result |
| EX-REG-01 | Registrar | Application plus duplicate/window denial | Application/status ID and safe denial |
| EX-REV-01 | Reviewer | Independent review/self-approval denial | Decision ID and maker-checker denial |
| EX-ADM-01 | Admin | Server 401/403 scope denial | Safe authorization result and audit reference |
| EX-AUD-01 | Auditor | Append-only audit/redaction inspection | Correlation ID and redaction check |
| EX-IMPORT-01 | Data Entry | Bad-file dry-run and recovery | Report ID and zero-write result |
| EX-CORRECT-01 | Reviewer | Effective-date correction/overlap denial | New event ID, date query and safe error |

**Exercise pass definition:** the trainer confirms the stated objective and evidence for the named exercise in an approved synthetic environment. `npm run test:training:exercises` proves only that the exercise pack and related local scripts are valid; it is not a trainee pass.

## Trainer record (blank by design)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Exercise ID / fixture | `________________` |
| Environment / build | `________________` |
| Trainee role and pseudonymous training ID | `________________` |
| Trainer role / name | `________________` |
| Evidence references | `________________` |
| Result | `PASS` / `RETRY` / `ESCALATE` |
| Trainer signature or approved e-signature reference | `________________` |
| Recorded at | `________________` |

An unsigned or evidence-less row is not an exercise pass or certification.
